at indfri.explanation: "At indfri" means "to fulfill / redeem". To say you keep a promise, use it with "et løfte" (a promise): "Hun indfrier sit løfte" (She fulfills her promise). To say you pay off a loan completely, use "et lån" (a loan): "Jeg vil indfri lånet" (I want to pay off the loan).

at indføre.explanation: "At indføre" means "to introduce (a rule)". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at føre" (to lead). To say a town starts new rules, use it with the rules: "Kommunen indfører nye regler" (The municipality is introducing new rules). To introduce one person to another, use "at præsentere" (to present): "Må jeg præsentere min ven?" (May I introduce my friend?).

at indgive.explanation: "At indgive" means "to submit / file". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at give" (to give). To say you hand an official application to an office, use it with "en ansøgning" (an application): "Hun indgav en ansøgning" (She submitted an application).

at indgå.explanation: "At indgå" means "to enter into (an agreement)". To say two people get married, use it with "ægteskab" (marriage): "De indgår ægteskab" (They are getting married). To say something is part of a whole, add "i" (in) after it: "Mel indgår i opskriften" (Flour is part of the recipe).

at indhente.explanation: "At indhente" means "to catch up with". To say you make up for lost time, use it with "det forsømte" (what was missed): "Jeg vil indhente det forsømte" (I want to make up for what was missed). To say you get quotes from companies, use it with "tilbud" (offers): "Vi indhenter tilbud" (We are getting quotes).

at indikere.explanation: "At indikere" means "to indicate". To say a measurement points toward a result, use it with "at" (that) after it: "Målingerne indikerer, at det bliver koldt" (The measurements indicate that it will be cold).

at indkalde.explanation: "At indkalde" means "to call in / summon". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at kalde" (to call). To say a court orders people to come, say: "Retten indkalder vidner" (The court summons witnesses). To say you call a meeting, add "til" (to) before it: "Jeg indkalder til møde" (I am calling a meeting).

at indkøbe.explanation: "At indkøbe" means "to purchase". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at købe" (to buy). To talk about everyday shopping, use "at købe ind" (to shop) instead: "Jeg skal købe ind i dag" (I have to go shopping today).

at indlede.explanation: "At indlede" means "to begin / introduce". To say someone opens a meeting, use it with "mødet" (the meeting): "Han indleder mødet" (He opens the meeting). To say you start a relationship, use it with "et forhold" (a relationship): "De indleder et forhold" (They are starting a relationship).

at indrette.explanation: "At indrette" means "to furnish / set up". To say you are furnishing a home, use it with the home: "De indretter lejligheden" (They are furnishing the flat). With "sig" (oneself) it means "to settle in": "Vi indretter os i den nye lejlighed" (We are settling in at the new flat).

at indrette sig.explanation: "At indrette sig" means "to adapt / settle in". To say you adapt to a situation, add "efter" (according to): "Vi må indrette os efter vejret" (We have to adapt to the weather). To say you settle in a new home, add "i" (in): "Hun indretter sig i huset" (She is settling in at the house). Without "sig" (oneself), "at indrette" means "to furnish": "Hun indretter værelset" (She is furnishing the room).

at indrømme.explanation: "At indrømme" means "to admit". To say you admit something, you can start with "Jeg må indrømme" (I have to admit): "Jeg må indrømme, at jeg tog fejl" (I have to admit that I was wrong).

at indsamle.explanation: "At indsamle" means "to collect". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at samle" (to gather). To talk about collecting as a hobby, use "at samle" instead: "Jeg samler på frimærker" (I collect stamps).

at indse.explanation: "At indse" means "to realize". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at se" (to see). To say you understood something too late, say: "Jeg indså for sent, at det var en fejl" (I realized too late that it was a mistake).

at indsende.explanation: "At indsende" means "to submit". It is built from "ind" (in) and "at sende" (to send). To say you send in an application, use it with "ansøgning" (application): "Jeg har indsendt min ansøgning" (I have submitted my application).

at indskrænke.explanation: "At indskrænke" means "to restrict". To say you cut down how much you spend, use it with "forbruget" (the spending): "Vi indskrænker forbruget" (We are cutting down spending). To say freedom is limited, use it with "friheden" (the freedom): "Loven indskrænker friheden" (The law restricts freedom).

at indstille.explanation: "At indstille" means "to adjust / set". To say you set a device, use it with the device: "Jeg indstiller uret" (I am setting the clock). To say you put someone forward for a job or prize, use it with "en kandidat" (a candidate): "De indstiller en kandidat" (They are nominating a candidate).

at indstille sig på.explanation: "At indstille sig på" means "to prepare for / adjust to". To say you get ready for something that is coming, say: "Vi må indstille os på en kold vinter" (We must prepare for a cold winter). To say you have accepted a change, say: "Jeg har indstillet mig på at flytte" (I have accepted that I will move).

at indsætte.explanation: "At indsætte" means "to insert / deposit". To say you put money into a bank account, say: "Jeg indsætter penge på kontoen" (I am depositing money in the account). To say you put something into a text, say: "Jeg indsætter et billede i teksten" (I am inserting a picture into the text). To take money out, use "at hæve" (to withdraw): "Jeg vil hæve tusind kroner" (I want to withdraw a thousand kroner).

at indtage.explanation: "At indtage" means "to consume / take". To say how medicine must be taken, say: "Medicinen skal indtages med vand" (The medicine must be taken with water). To say soldiers capture a place, say: "Soldaterne indtog byen" (The soldiers captured the town).

at informere.explanation: "At informere" means "to inform". To name the topic, add "om" (about) before it: "Jeg informerer dig om mødet" (I am informing you about the meeting).

at insistere.explanation: "At insistere" means "to insist". To say what you insist on, add "på" (on) before it: "Jeg insisterer på en undskyldning" (I insist on an apology).

at inspirere.explanation: "At inspirere" means "to inspire". To say a book gave you ideas, say: "Bogen inspirerede mig" (The book inspired me). To say you were inspired by something, use "at blive inspireret af" (to be inspired by): "Jeg blev inspireret af filmen" (I was inspired by the film).

at installere.explanation: "At installere" means "to install". To ask someone to install a program, say: "Kan du installere appen?" (Can you install the app?). To say you remove it again, add "af" (off) to the front: "Jeg afinstallerer spillet" (I am uninstalling the game).

at integrere.explanation: "At integrere" means "to integrate". To say newcomers are made part of a society, say: "at integrere flygtninge" (to integrate refugees). To say you become part of a group yourself, add "sig" (oneself): "Han har integreret sig godt" (He has integrated well).
